AGENCY ADOPTION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Casey Morgan · Riley Lee

DECLARATION OF PURPOSE — AGENCY ADOPTION INFORMATION SHEET
This Agency Adoption — Information Sheet describes California's statutory process for Riley Lee (born April 3, 2019) to be relinquished by Casey Morgan, the child's birth parent, to Sacramento County Adoption Agency — the California State Department of Social Services, a county adoption agency, or a licensed adoption agency — for adoptive placement, and ultimately for adoption by Jordan Lee, under California Family Code Division 13, Part 2, Chapter 2 (Agency Adoptions, §§ 8700–8720). It is prepared for use alongside an actual agency adoption contemplated for filing in the California superior court for Sacramento County.

An agency adoption is its own distinct statutory track, defined by whether the department, a county adoption agency, or a licensed adoption agency is itself a party to, or joins in, the adoption petition — separate from an independent adoption under Family Code Chapter 3 (§§ 8800–8823), in which the birth parent personally selects the prospective adoptive parent and no agency joins the petition, and separate from a stepparent adoption under Family Code Chapter 5 (§§ 9000–9007), which applies only where the person adopting is the spouse or domestic partner of the child's existing legal parent.

This information sheet is not itself a court filing. Completing it does not relinquish Riley Lee to Sacramento County Adoption Agency, does not terminate any parent's rights, does not accept or record any relinquishment, and does not determine that any specific adoption should or will be granted. Only the statutory relinquishment process and a final court decree of adoption, entered after the process described in this document's companion clauses, can actually do that.

STATUTORY DEFINITION OF "AGENCY ADOPTION," AND THE THREE KINDS OF AGENCIES
California's adoption statutes define what makes an adoption an agency adoption by reference to who is a party to the adoption petition. Family Code § 8506 provides that “Agency adoption” means the adoption of a minor, other than an intercountry adoption, in which the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency is a party to, or joins in, the adoption petition.” The statutory chapter that governs this process — Family Code Division 13, Part 2, Chapter 2, captioned “Agency Adoptions” and running from § 8700 through § 8720 — consistently refers to three distinct kinds of agencies that may receive a relinquished child: “the department” (the State Department of Social Services), a “county adoption agency,” and a “licensed adoption agency” (a private agency licensed by the department). Sacramento County Adoption Agency is identified in this document as the agency to which Riley Lee is relinquished under this chapter.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "“Agency adoption” means the adoption of a minor, other than an intercountry adoption, in which the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency is a party to, or joins in, the adoption petition."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8506 (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8506 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8506.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of how California law itself defines an agency adoption and identifies the agencies that chapter covers — not a claim about which state's law would govern any specific adoption, and not a claim that the relinquishment or adoption described in this document's companion clauses has been, or will be, classified by any court as an agency adoption within the meaning of § 8506. Family Code § 8506 sits in Division 13, Part 1 (Definitions, §§ 8500–8548), a separate part from the Chapter 2 sections (§§ 8700–8720) this document otherwise draws on; this is a single statutory section, and no additional independent source was found for the definition itself. This clause does not further detail Family Code § 8524's separate definition of “independent adoption” (already addressed in this corpus's Independent Adoption document), or the licensing requirements a private agency must satisfy to become a “licensed adoption agency” under Division 13. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine that Sacramento County Adoption Agency is a department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency within the meaning of § 8506 in any specific case.

HOW A BIRTH PARENT RELINQUISHES A CHILD TO AN AGENCY
Family Code § 8700(a) sets out the basic mechanics by which a birth parent relinquishes a child to an agency for adoption: “Either birth parent may relinquish a child to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency for adoption by a written statement signed before two subscribing witnesses and acknowledged before an authorized official of the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency.” The same subdivision gives the signed relinquishment evidentiary weight on the question of custody: when it recites that the signing parent is entitled to the child's sole custody and is acknowledged before the officer, it is “prima facie evidence of the right of the person making it to the sole custody of the child and the person’s sole right to relinquish.” Section 8700 separately addresses relinquishment by a minor parent, and by a parent (or a parent and child) residing outside California, in subdivisions (b) through (d), which this clause does not detail.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "(a) Either birth parent may relinquish a child to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency for adoption by a written statement signed before two subscribing witnesses and acknowledged before an authorized official of the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency. The relinquishment, when reciting that the person making it is entitled to the sole custody of the child and acknowledged before the officer, is prima facie evidence of the right of the person making it to the sole custody of the child and the person’s sole right to relinquish."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the relinquishment procedure a birth parent follows under California's agency-adoption chapter — not a claim about which state's law would govern any specific relinquishment, and not a claim that Casey Morgan has signed, or will sign, a relinquishment described in this clause. This is a single statutory section (§ 8700); its subdivisions (b), (c), and (d) — addressing a minor relinquishing parent and a parent or child residing outside California — are not detailed in this clause, and are addressed separately (subdivisions (e) through (h)) in this document's companion clauses on the revocation period and named-placement rescission. This document is informational only: it does not itself constitute a relinquishment, does not witness or acknowledge any signature, and does not determine that any relinquishment described in this document's companion clauses satisfies § 8700's requirements in any specific case.

WHEN A RELINQUISHMENT BECOMES FINAL, AND RESCISSION BY MUTUAL CONSENT AFTERWARD
A signed relinquishment does not become legally final the moment it is signed. Family Code § 8700(e)(1) provides that “[t]he relinquishment authorized by this section has no effect until a certified copy is sent to, and filed with, the department.” The same subdivision separately provides that the agency must inform the birth parent that the birth parent may request withdrawal during the interval before that filing. Once filed, “[t]he relinquishment shall be final 10 business days after receipt of the filing by the department, unless any of the following applies: (A) The department sends written acknowledgment of receipt of the relinquishment prior to the expiration of that 10-day period, at which time the relinquishment shall be final. (B) A longer period of time is necessary due to a pending court action or some other cause beyond control of the department. (C) The birth parent signs a waiver of right to revoke relinquishment pursuant to Section 8700.5, in which case the relinquishment shall become final as provided in that section.” After that point, § 8700(e)(2) provides that “[a]fter the relinquishment is final, it may be rescinded only by the mutual consent of the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency to which the child was relinquished and the birth parent or parents relinquishing the child” — meaning a birth parent cannot unilaterally undo a final relinquishment under this subdivision.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The relinquishment shall be final 10 business days after receipt of the filing by the department, unless any of the following applies: (A) The department sends written acknowledgment of receipt of the relinquishment prior to the expiration of that 10-day period, at which time the relinquishment shall be final. (B) A longer period of time is necessary due to a pending court action or some other cause beyond control of the department. (C) The birth parent signs a waiver of right to revoke relinquishment pursuant to Section 8700.5, in which case the relinquishment shall become final as provided in that section."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(e)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(e)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  "After the relinquishment is final, it may be rescinded only by the mutual consent of the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency to which the child was relinquished and the birth parent or parents relinquishing the child."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(e)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(e)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the specific finality timeline and mutual-consent rescission rule California law applies to a relinquishment under this chapter — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific relinquishment, or about what revocation period, if any, another state's process allows, and not a claim that any relinquishment described in this document's companion clauses has been, will be, filed, finalized, or rescinded in any specific case. Family Code § 8700(e)(1) and (e)(2) are subdivisions of the same statutory section as § 8700(a), cited separately in this document's companion clause on relinquishment procedure; they are treated here as one statutory source, not as independent corroboration of one another. This clause does not independently verify Family Code § 8700.5 (the waiver-of-right-to-revoke procedure cross-referenced in subdivision (e)(1)(C)), and does not detail the separate, later-arising rescission right for a named-placement relinquishment addressed in this document's companion clause on named-placement rescission. This document is informational only: it does not itself calculate whether any specific 10-business-day period has run, and does not rescind, withdraw, or finalize any relinquishment.

A SEPARATE 30-DAY RESCISSION RIGHT WHEN A NAMED PLACEMENT FALLS THROUGH
The relinquishment chapter gives a birth parent an additional, later-arising rescission right tied to a specific circumstance: a relinquishment naming particular prospective adoptive parents that is not followed through on. Family Code § 8700(f) provides that “[t]he relinquishing parent may name in the relinquishment the person or persons with whom the relinquishing parent intends that placement of the child for adoption be made by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency.” Section 8700(g) then provides that, notwithstanding the finality rule in subdivision (e), “if the relinquishment names the person or persons with whom placement by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency is intended and the child is not placed in the home of the named person or persons or the child is removed from the home prior to the granting of the adoption, the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency shall mail a notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the birth parent signing the relinquishment within 72 hours of the decision not to place the child for adoption or the decision to remove the child from the home.” Once that notice issues, § 8700(h) provides that “[t]he relinquishing parent has 30 days from the date on which the notice described in subdivision (g) was mailed to rescind the relinquishment.”

  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(f) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(f) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  "if the relinquishment names the person or persons with whom placement by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency is intended and the child is not placed in the home of the named person or persons or the child is removed from the home prior to the granting of the adoption, the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency shall mail a notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the birth parent signing the relinquishment within 72 hours of the decision not to place the child for adoption or the decision to remove the child from the home."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(g) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(g) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  "The relinquishing parent has 30 days from the date on which the notice described in subdivision (g) was mailed to rescind the relinquishment."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8700(h) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8700(h) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8700.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of a specific, circumstance-triggered rescission right that applies only to a named-placement relinquishment under California's agency-adoption chapter — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific relinquishment, and not a claim that Riley Lee's relinquishment (if any) named Jordan Lee or any other person, or that the triggering circumstance in § 8700(g) has occurred, in any specific case. Family Code § 8700(f), (g), and (h) are subdivisions of the same statutory section already cited in this document's companion clauses on relinquishment procedure and the general revocation period; they are treated here as one statutory source. This clause does not detail § 8700(h)'s further paragraphs (not reached in the text reviewed for this document) on what happens if the relinquishing parent does not request rescission within the 30-day period, or on identifying a different named person during that period; it also does not address § 8700(i) through (k), covering a relinquishment tied to a Welfare and Institutions Code § 361 dependency proceeding, the termination-of-rights effect of filing, and the department's regulatory authority. This document is informational only: it does not itself mail any notice, does not calculate whether any specific 30-day period has run, and does not rescind any relinquishment.

THE AGENCY'S EXCLUSIVE CUSTODY PENDING AN ADOPTION ORDER, AND WHO MAY PETITION
Once a child is freed for adoption, the agency — not the birth parent or the prospective adoptive parents — holds legal custody until a court grants the adoption. Family Code § 8704(a) provides that the agency “to which a child has been freed for adoption by either relinquishment or termination of parental rights is responsible for the care of the child, and is entitled to the exclusive custody and control of the child until an order of adoption is granted.” Consistent with that exclusive role, § 8704(b) restricts who may file the adoption petition itself: “No petition may be filed to adopt a child relinquished to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency or a child declared free from the custody and control of either or both birth parents and referred to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency for adoptive placement, except by the prospective adoptive parents with whom the child has been placed for adoption by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency.” The same subdivision also gives a court a check on an agency's refusal to consent to the adoption by the family it placed the child with: “If the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency refuses to consent to the adoption of a child by the person or persons with whom the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency placed the child for adoption, the court may nevertheless order the adoption if it finds that the refusal to consent is not in the child’s best interest.”

  "No petition may be filed to adopt a child relinquished to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency or a child declared free from the custody and control of either or both birth parents and referred to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency for adoptive placement, except by the prospective adoptive parents with whom the child has been placed for adoption by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8704(b) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8704(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8704.)
  "If the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency refuses to consent to the adoption of a child by the person or persons with whom the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency placed the child for adoption, the court may nevertheless order the adoption if it finds that the refusal to consent is not in the child’s best interest."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8704(b) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8704(b), court-override sentence (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8704.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the agency's custodial role pending an adoption order and of who may file the adoption petition under California's agency-adoption chapter — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific placement or petition, and not a claim that Jordan Lee has been, or will be, the prospective adoptive parent with whom Riley Lee is placed for adoption in any specific case. Family Code § 8704(a) and (b) are subdivisions of the same statutory section, treated here as one source. This clause omits § 8704(b)'s middle sentence, addressing an agency's removal of a placed child with court approval after the petition is filed and on a supported motion — a related but separate procedure this document does not detail. This document is informational only: it does not itself place, remove, or grant custody of any child, does not file any adoption petition, and does not determine whether any agency's consent or refusal to consent, or any court's best-interest finding, applies in any specific case.

THE AGENCY'S REPORT TO THE COURT
Before a California court can grant an agency adoption, the agency itself must report to the court on the case. Family Code § 8715(a) provides that “[t]he department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency, whichever is a party to, or joins in, the petition, shall submit a full report of the facts of the case to the court.” This report requirement sits within the same chapter as the filing rules for the adoption request (Family Code § 8714), and applies regardless of which of the three kinds of agencies identified in this document's companion clause on the statutory definition of agency adoption — the department, a county adoption agency, or a licensed adoption agency — is the party to, or joins in, Jordan Lee's adoption petition for Riley Lee.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency, whichever is a party to, or joins in, the petition, shall submit a full report of the facts of the case to the court."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 8715(a) (California Legislative Information text), Fam. C. § 8715(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=8715.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of the agency-report requirement California law imposes before an agency adoption may be granted — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific adoption proceeding, and not a claim that any report described in this clause has been, or will be, submitted for Riley Lee's adoption in any specific case. This is a single statutory section (§ 8715); its subdivisions (b) through (e) — addressing additional report content required when a child was freed for adoption from juvenile-court dependency, a postadoption contact agreement, an optional department report, and an out-of-state petitioner's home-study report — are not detailed in this clause. This clause also does not detail Family Code § 8714's separate filing requirements for the adoption request itself (where to file, the court clerk's notice duty to the department, and the contents of the petition and order), which this document does not otherwise cover. This document is informational only: it does not itself submit any report to any court, and does not determine the contents or sufficiency of any report filed in any specific case.

expectedJSON.body: Once a child is freed for adoption, the agency — not the birth parent or the prospective adoptive parents — holds legal custody until a court grants the adoption. Family Code § 8704(a) provides that the agency “to which a child has been freed for adoption by either relinquishment or termination of parental rights is responsible for the care of the child, and is entitled to the exclusive custody and control of the child until an order of adoption is granted.” Consistent with that exclusive role, § 8704(b) restricts who may file the adoption petition itself: “No petition may be filed to adopt a child relinquished to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency or a child declared free from the custody and control of either or both birth parents and referred to the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency for adoptive placement, except by the prospective adoptive parents with whom the child has been placed for adoption by the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency.” The same subdivision also gives a court a check on an agency's refusal to consent to the adoption by the family it placed the child with: “If the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency refuses to consent to the adoption of a child by the person or persons with whom the department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency placed the child for adoption, the court may nevertheless order the adoption if it finds that the refusal to consent is not in the child’s best interest.”

Family Code § 8715(a) provides that “[t]he department, county adoption agency, or licensed adoption agency, whichever is a party to, or joins in, the petition, shall submit a full report of the facts of the case to the court.” This report requirement sits within the same chapter as the filing rules for the adoption request (Family Code § 8714), and applies regardless of which of the three kinds of agencies identified in this document's companion clause on the statutory definition of agency adoption — the department, a county adoption agency, or a licensed adoption agency — is the party to, or joins in, Jordan Lee's adoption petition for Riley Lee.
